questions.question: I ______ that film last week, but I can hardly remember the plot.
options: A. see
B. saw
C. have seen
D. had seen
questions.explanation: Past simple is used for a completed action at a specific past time ('last week'). 'Have seen' would require no time reference or a period up to now; 'had seen' needs an earlier past event; 'see' is present.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: We ______ the client at 3 PM tomorrow, so please prepare the documents.
options: A. meet
B. are meeting
C. have met
D. met
questions.explanation: Present continuous is used for a fixed future arrangement. 'Meet' is present simple (habitual), 'have met' is present perfect, 'met' is past simple – none express future arrangement.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: By the time we arrived at the cinema, the film ______, so we missed the opening scene.
options: A. started
B. has started
C. had started
D. starts
questions.explanation: Past perfect ('had started') is used for an action completed before another past action ('arrived'). 'Started' would imply simultaneous actions; 'has started' is present perfect; 'starts' is present simple.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: She ______ to school by bus every day, but today she is walking.
options: A. goes
B. is going
C. has gone
D. went
questions.explanation: Present simple expresses a habitual action ('every day'). 'Is going' is present continuous (current action), 'has gone' is present perfect (completed), 'went' is past simple – none fit the habitual context.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: He opened the door, ______ a strange figure in the corridor, and immediately felt a chill.
options: A. sees
B. saw
C. has seen
D. had seen
questions.explanation: In a narrative, maintain past tense consistency. 'Opened' and 'felt' are past simple; 'saw' matches. 'Sees' is present, 'has seen' is present perfect, 'had seen' would indicate an earlier action – all break the tense sequence.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: She ______ for three hours, so she feels exhausted now.
options: A. has studied
B. has been studying
C. studied
D. studies
questions.explanation: Present perfect continuous emphasises the duration of an action that has just finished and has a present result. 'Has studied' focuses on completion without duration; 'studied' is past simple; 'studies' is present simple – none convey the ongoing nature up to now.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: By next month, I ______ the project, so I can submit it to the manager.
options: A. will complete
B. will have completed
C. am completing
D. have completed
questions.explanation: Future perfect ('will have completed') expresses an action that will be finished before a specific future time ('by next month'). 'Will complete' is simple future, 'am completing' is present continuous, 'have completed' is present perfect – none indicate completion by a future deadline.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: If I ______ about the meeting earlier, I would have rearranged my schedule.
options: A. knew
B. had known
C. know
D. have known
questions.explanation: This is a third conditional: past perfect ('had known') in the if-clause, and 'would have + past participle' in the main clause. 'Knew' is past simple (second conditional), 'know' is present, 'have known' is present perfect – all form incorrect conditional structures.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the zero conditional?
options: A. If water reaches 100°C, it boils.
B. If water reaches 100°C, it will boil.
C. If water reached 100°C, it would boil.
D. If water has reached 100°C, it boiled.
questions.explanation: Zero conditional states general truths or scientific facts. Both clauses use present simple: 'if + present simple, present simple'. Option B is first conditional (future), C is second (hypothetical), D is incorrect tense.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct first conditional sentence for a real possibility.
options: A. If it will rain tomorrow, we cancel the picnic.
B. If it rains tomorrow, we will cancel the picnic.
C. If it rained tomorrow, we would cancel the picnic.
D. If it had rained tomorrow, we would have cancelled the picnic.
questions.explanation: First conditional: 'if + present simple, will + base verb' for real future possibilities. Option A uses 'will' in the if-clause (incorrect), C is second conditional, D is third.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence is a correct second conditional?
options: A. If I have more time, I will help you.
B. If I had more time, I would help you.
C. If I had had more time, I would have helped you.
D. If I would have more time, I helped you.
questions.explanation: Second conditional for hypothetical present/future: 'if + past simple, would + base verb'. Option A is first, C is third, D uses 'would' in the if-clause (incorrect).
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which mixed conditional correctly expresses a past condition with a present result?
options: A. If I took that job, I would be rich now.
B. If I had taken that job, I would be rich now.
C. If I had taken that job, I would have been rich now.
D. If I take that job, I will be rich now.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: past condition (if + past perfect) + present result (would + base verb). Option A uses past simple (wrong tense), C is third conditional, D is first.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence using 'unless' in a first conditional.
options: A. Unless it rains, we will go to the beach.
B. Unless it will rain, we will go to the beach.
C. Unless it rained, we would go to the beach.
D. Unless it had rained, we would have gone to the beach.
questions.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not'. First conditional: 'unless + present simple, will + base verb'. Option B uses 'will' after unless (incorrect), C is second, D is third.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Select the correct negative third conditional.
options: A. If he hadn't missed the bus, he wouldn't be late.
B. If he hadn't missed the bus, he wouldn't have been late.
C. If he didn't miss the bus, he wouldn't have been late.
D. If he wouldn't have missed the bus, he wouldn't have been late.
questions.explanation: Third conditional negative: 'if + hadn't + past participle, would have + past participle'. Option A is mixed (past condition, present result), C uses past simple, D uses 'would' in if-clause.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which mixed conditional correctly expresses a present condition with a past result?
options: A. If I were taller, I would have become a basketball player.
B. If I had been taller, I would become a basketball player.
C. If I am taller, I would have become a basketball player.
D. If I were taller, I would become a basketball player.
questions.explanation: Mixed conditional: present condition (if + past simple/were) + past result (would have + past participle). Option B is past condition + present result, C mixes tenses, D is second conditional.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Identify the correct inversion in a conditional sentence.
options: A. Had I known about the meeting, I would have attended.
B. If I had known about the meeting, I would attend.
C. Were I known about the meeting, I would have attended.
D. Had I known about the meeting, I would attend.
questions.explanation: Inversion in third conditional: 'Had + subject + past participle' replaces 'If + subject + had'. Option A is correct: past condition + past result. B uses 'if' (no inversion) but wrong result, C is ungrammatical, D mixes past condition with present result.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: After he ______ his homework, he went out to play with his friends.
options: A. was finishing
B. has finished
C. had finished
D. finishes
questions.explanation: The past perfect ('had finished') shows the homework was completed before the past action 'went out'. 'Was finishing' describes an action still in progress at that past moment; 'has finished' is present perfect and 'finishes' is present simple, neither of which fits a past narrative.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Identify the correct third conditional sentence.
options: A. If she studied, she will pass the exam.
B. If she had studied, she would pass the exam.
C. If she had studied, she would have passed the exam.
D. If she studied, she would have passed the exam.
questions.explanation: Third conditional for past unreal: 'if + past perfect, would have + past participle'. Option B is a grammatical mixed conditional (past condition, present result) but not third conditional. Option A wrongly pairs a past-tense if-clause with a first-conditional result ('will pass'). Option D mixes a second-conditional if-clause with a third-conditional result.
questions.subject: english

questions.question: Which sentence uses the subjunctive 'were' correctly in a second conditional?
options: A. If I was you, I would apologize.
B. If I were you, I would apologize.
C. If I had been you, I would apologize.
D. If I am you, I would apologize.
questions.explanation: In the second conditional, the subjunctive 'were' is used for all persons in formal standard English. Option A uses 'was', which appears in informal speech but is not the subjunctive form. Option C is a mixed conditional (a third-conditional if-clause with a second-conditional result). Option D incorrectly combines a present-simple if-clause with 'would', matching neither the first nor the second conditional pattern.
questions.subject: english
